title: Replace or Augment: Rethinking the Role of Learned Indexes in Relational Databases
abstract: B-Trees are the predominant index structures in relational databases. However, they become a performance bottleneck in traversal-heavy workloads. Although learned indexes have emerged as a promising solution to mitigate this bottleneck, their high engineering complexity hinders their practical adoption as replacements for B-Trees. Instead, we propose a more viable alternative: augmenting B-Trees with learned indexing techniques to reduce integration costs and speed up traversals. To this end, we present MirrorBtr, a unified framework that builds upon existing learned indexes to accelerate B-Tree traversals without altering the B-Tree structure. MirrorBtr reduces space and synchronization overhead and dynamically adapts to B-Tree updates. We implement MirrorBtr in MySQL InnoDB and conduct extensive evaluations, showing that it consistently delivers traversal speedups with negligible maintenance overhead and outperforms both the conventional B-Tree and prior acceleration methods in InnoDB. In particular, MirrorBtr achieves up to 7.45× higher query throughput than the B-Tree.
